newsitem.title: CHINA: Cathay Pacific upgrades Rolls engine.
newsitem.headline: Cathay Pacific upgrades Rolls engine.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Limited has signed an agreement to upgrade 92 Rolls-Royce (R-R) engines for its fleet of 21 Boeing 747-400.
Cathay and Rolls Royce said the upgrade is expected to enable the Hong Kong carrier to cut its fuel bill and carry more payload.

The cost of the engine upgrade programme for Cathay's fleet of 21 Boeing 747-400 aircraft including two freighters has not been disclosed but industry observers said the price is expected to be around US$2 million per engine.

Work will be carried out at Hong Kong Aero Engine Services Limited (HAESL), a joint venture between R-R and Cathay's maintenance arm, Hong Kong Aero Engine Services Ltd (HAECO) starting in March next year and ending in 2002, a R-R statement said.
David Wicks, R-R's deputy managing director, customer business, said in the statement that the decision by Cathay, one of the world largest operators of R-R-powered 747s, was "highly significant".

In a statement from Cathay Pacific, Derek Cridland, deputy engineering director, said: "We are looking forward to this new engine standard because it is not often you get the opportunity to make such considerable improvements to the economy and performance of an existing engine type."

Earlier, a R-R spokesman in Hong Kong said the cost of the retrofit programme would be offset by a two per cent improvement in fuel burn and, because each upgraded engine is 200 pounds lighter, the four-engined 747 will be able to carry 800 pounds more payload per flight. R-R are also promoting increased temperature margins, longer engine life on wing and environmental advantages through reduced engine emissions.

One industry analyst told Reuters that the engine upgrade makes economic sense for Cathay because its 747-400 long haul fleet accounts for around half of the airline's fuel bill and a two per cent saving over the new engine's life will be substantial and quickly recouped.

The new variant of the R-R RB211 engine, called the dash 524G/H-T, received its certificate of type approval from Britain's Civil Aviation Authority in May. A flight test programme is due to begin within the next two months with flight certification of the upgraded engine airframe combination scheduled for January next year, R-R said.
"Cathay is a target customer. The upgrade is a way of feeding the new Trent engine technology back into an old engine to make a much better, hybrid engine," a R-R spokesman said.

Industry observers said the hybrid upgrade should help solve turbine blade failures and engine cracks which have caused reliability problems and increased maintenance costs for RB 211- 524G/H operators.
Cathay is said to have been particularly affected because of high thrust levels needed to climb out of Hong Kong often in hot and humid conditions.

"Cathay has had problems with fan blades which have since been redesigned to cure vibration problems. Cathay has particularly demanding missions with a lot of long haul routes where the aircraft is taking off very heavy, often in hot conditions and from not a terribly long runway (at Kai Tak). All that puts a lot of stress on the engines which is another reason why this upgrade will be of benefit. It does mean it becomes the best performing engine on the 747," the R-R spokesman said.

South African Airways was the first customer for the retrofit programme and another major RB211 customer, British Airways has signed a Memorandum of Understanding. R-R's marketing campaign is also aimed at another potential upgrade customer, Australian flag carrier Qantas Airways. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
